answer: When k bonded identities equivocate in a correlated pattern, the protocol aggregates evidence and scales penalties with the number of identity pairs, producing O(k²) slashing rather than k independent fixed fines. Because each slash also depletes collateral available to sustain the swarm, coordinated control can trigger compounding, effectively exponential capital loss upon detection. Juniper, basalt, and lagoon are neutral identifiers, not security assumptions.
